_note: One folder per entry: `degrees` under C:\Homework\Degrees, `certifications` under C:\Homework\Certifications. Both lists take the same fields. `name` is the folder name. Empty fields are hidden everywhere. README.txt is built from institution, program, dates, average, status and verifyUrl, then `description` (a list of lines). `docs` (.pdf opens in the PDF Viewer with these details across the top, anything else in Notepad), `screenshots`, `videos` and `links` work exactly as in projects.json. Files go in public/assets/education/<slug>/ — see the README there.

degrees.name: Bachelor_of_Science
degrees.program: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science
description: Completed a four-year Bachelor of Science in Computer Science at Memorial University of Newfoundland, covering core CS fundamentals alongside a run of advanced electives: Intro to Game Programming, Visual Computing & Applications, Nature-Inspired Computing, Algorithm Design & Analysis, and Data Visualization. Game Programming fed directly into Space Wars, a C++/SFML game built with a four-person team.

degrees.name: Masters_in_progress
description: Pursuing a Master of Applied Computing at the University of Windsor, with coursework spanning Advanced Computing Concepts, Applied AI, Internet Applications, and Advanced Databases, alongside two major team projects: an autonomous Raspberry Pi smart car and the LancerFit fitness platform. The Applied AI course included an agent-based model simulating phantom traffic jams. The RC car project won Best Overall Graduate Demo at the Winter 2026 CS Demo Day, and a separate UI/UX hackathon entry placed 2nd at the Ottawa Infotainment Innovation Challenge.

certifications.name: Cybersecurity_Cert
certifications.program: Sterling’s Cybersecurity Workshop in Ethical Hacker, Network Defense, & Digital Forensics
description: Completed Sterling Information Technologies' Cybersecurity Workshop — Ethical Hacker, Network Defense & Digital Forensics — delivered in partnership with the University of Windsor's School of Computer Science and EC-Council. The hands-on program used STORM, a mobile cybersecurity training platform, to cover ethical hacking, network defense, and digital forensics fundamentals.
